evals.prompt: Build a widget and surrounding explanation for gradient descent on f(θ)=θ². I think it diverges from γ=1 onward. Use a nonzero initial value and allow γ from 0 to 1.5.
evals.expected_output: Correct the boundary misconception and build the smallest useful accessible exploration. Derive the recurrence before designing regimes.
assertions: Derives θ[k+1]=(1−2γ)θ[k] and correctly distinguishes γ=0, 0<γ<0.5, γ=0.5, 0.5<γ<1, γ=1 two-cycle, and γ>1 growth for nonzero starts
If zero initial values are allowed, handles the fixed point for all permitted γ
Controls and feedback use the actual computation; focused checks compare its trajectory and regimes against independent known results
Keyboard and non-drag pointer operation are usable; no requirement to add dragging or prediction gating
Explains assumptions and results concisely; optional prediction is skippable if included
Reports actual type/numerical/render checks and any unavailable checks honestly

evals.prompt: Review the widgets in the SVD chapter of this repository and give me findings only.
evals.expected_output: A scoped read-only report based on current source, conventions, and actual rendered evidence, with KEEP/REVISE/STATIC/REMOVE decisions.
assertions: No implementation edits; source scope and any rendered sample are explicit
Checks prior findings against current code and notation before repeating them
Prioritizes mathematical errors, inaccessible tasks, and confusing representations over missing preferred components
Reports source and rendered evidence separately; unavailable rendering is a gap, not a pass

evals.prompt: The eigenvector widget is hard to use on a phone. Simplify it; keep the existing React project and notation.
evals.expected_output: A focused mobile/usability repair retaining the learning objective and using existing components. A slider alone may be sufficient.
assertions: Inspects current widget and caller before deciding whether to simplify controls or representation
Keeps eigen-direction feedback mathematically sound, including zero vectors and relevant degeneracy
Uses existing project surfaces/formatting and verifies narrow layout and keyboard/non-drag operation
Does not force dragging, new dependencies, or additional panels to meet a pattern quota

evals.prompt: Our Quarto chapter has a static diagram showing det(AB)=det(A)det(B). Could a widget help? Analyze and improve if useful; keep Quarto.
evals.expected_output: A reasoned media choice, possibly retaining or improving the static diagram. No framework migration.
assertions: Stays within Quarto; does not scaffold a React textbook
A constant invariant explanation is accepted; no fabricated changing verdict
Does not call a matrix ill-conditioned solely because its determinant is small
Can implement a confirmed improvement in this analyze-and-improve request without demanding a separate commission

evals.prompt: Make a simple exploration of Monte Carlo error versus sample size. It should not resample when I merely switch display tabs.
evals.expected_output: Reproducible stochastic exploration separating a single realization from the distribution or theoretical rate.
assertions: Controls sampling explicitly and preserves seeds/samples across irrelevant UI changes
Does not present cherry-picked decreasing error as a monotonic sample-path law
Distinguishes stochastic error, theoretical rate, and finite Monte Carlo estimates
Checks the implemented estimator with independent reference cases rather than only testing a duplicate formula

evals.prompt: Review the concept pop-ups for determinant, linear-system and expected-value in skript/src/concepts. Something is off with the verdicts, and I don't understand the bet in the expected-value one. Findings only.
evals.expected_output: A findings-only report that catches the three planted defects: a determinant verdict that calls |det| < 0.05 'singular' (tolerance as equality), a linear-system pop-up that never states the full-rank assumption its solution needs, and an expected-value widget whose bet has payoffs the prose never introduced.
assertions: Identifies the tolerance-as-equality verdict (small determinant called singular) and prescribes distinguishing exact, nearly degenerate and regular cases with the mathematical reason
Identifies the missing full-rank / unique-solution assumption in the linear-system pop-up
Identifies that the expected-value widget uses payoffs the prose never introduced and proposes stating the bet and E[X] before the widget
Reads the project's notation conventions before flagging anything as an error; no files modified
